subject: ClearHarbor: operational assurance package and 30-day remediation cadence
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearharbor.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearharbor.com
Date: 2026-09-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes this week - initial impact summary

Kimberly —

We saw three sustained degradation windows yesterday and two brief spikes this morning across our inference endpoints (predominantly /v1/generate). Median p95 latency jumped from ~150ms to ~1.2s for the 10:45–11:03 UTC window. Error rates (5xx) peaked at 4.6% for that period; throughput throttled for a handful of mid-size batch jobs. This is materially impacting our interactive UI conversions.

Can you share what root cause analysis you have and a concrete remediation timeline? Our procurement team is already asking about credits. We need an operational assurance package and a 30-day cadence for fixes and verification.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearHarbor
[Phone: +1-415-555-0142]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearharbor.com>

Date: 2026-09-19T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes this week - immediate next steps

Samir —

Really sorry for the disruption. I’ve looped in Rishi and Marissa (on-call infra + runtime) and Laura (customer success) so we can get you a concrete RCA and an operational cadence by end of day tomorrow. Immediate actions we’re taking:

- Rishi is running a targeted query over kv cache hot-keys and kernel selection telemetry to identify misrouted requests.
- We’ve raised a high-priority JIRA (JIRA-OPS-1287) for the incident and scheduled an internal bridge at 10:30 PT.
- Temporary mitigation: we will pin ClearHarbor to the lower-latency model variant (rwd-llama-13b-lat) for the next 72 hours and enable aggressive prefix caching for frequently repeated prompts.

I will also prepare an operational assurance package (RCA summary, patch plan, test checklist) and propose a 30-day remediation cadence with weekly checkpoints. Laura will follow up on credits/questions from procurement.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-19T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: recurring latency spikes this week - preliminary technical findings

Team —

Summary of initial findings from the bridge and trace aggregation:

- Root cause (probable): A KV-cache index corruption combined with a non-ideal kernel selector path for rwd-llama-13b variants under mixed short/long sequence patterns. This triggered repeated cache-miss storms that ballooned decode time and increased lock contention in the runtime batcher.
- Evidence: increased KV miss-rate correlated with host-level GPU queue depth spikes (see attached traces). Sampling of request IDs (HS-98234) shows that long-context requests were sometimes routed to smaller-kernel paths causing full-cache rebuilds.
- Immediate mitigation applied: pinned ClearHarbor to rwd-llama-13b-lat variant and enabled conservative batching (max batch size 8) + prefix-only KV caching. Error rates returned to baseline within 18 minutes.

Planned corrective actions:
1) Hot-fix: KV-cache index repair and stronger validation on cache insert/remove (deployable within 48 hours) — patch attached (kv_cache_patch.diff).
2) Medium-term: kernel-selector gating to ensure sequence-length-aware routing and tighter telemetry for route-churn (2-week sprint).
3) Validation: canary test harness against synthetic ClearHarbor traffic and weekly perf regression checks for 30 days.

I’ll assemble the full RCA PDF and a remediation cadence spreadsheet for Kimberly to send to the customer.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rwd-traces-20260919.zip (referenced)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, procurement@clearharbor.com, Jessica Lang <jessica@ops-consulting.io>
Date: 2026-09-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: ClearHarbor RCA and 30-day remediation cadence (delivery)

Samir / Procurement team —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is the customer-ready RCA and our proposed 30-day remediation cadence (summary below). We take outages like this seriously; our goal is zero surprise regressions and demonstrable verification you can use in your runbook.

Executive summary:
- Incident: repeated latency spikes and elevated 5xx rates on 2026-09-18/19 caused by KV-cache index corruption combined with sequence-length misrouting to inefficient kernel paths.
- Impact: peak p95 increased to ~1.2s; 5xx spiked to 4.6%; some batched ingest jobs experienced throughput degradation.
- Fixes: hot-fix patch (kv_cache_patch.diff) to repair and harden KV index; conservative routing/gating changes; canary test harness.

30-day remediation cadence (high-level):
- Week 0 (this week): apply hot-fix to ClearHarbor tearrun cluster (done in maintenance window), enable aggressive prefix caching.
- Week 1: deploy kernel-selector gating across Blue/Green, run synthetic traffic canaries and capture p95/p99 baselines.
- Week 2: integrate route-churn telemetry; start weekly perf regression jobs.
- Weeks 3–4: operational verification and SLA adjustment (if needed); final sign-off call and runbook handover.

We propose weekly checkpoint calls (Thursdays, 15:00 PT) for the next 30 days. I’ve attached: clearharbor_rca.pdf (full RCA), kv_cache_patch.diff (hot-fix), and 30-day-remediation-cadence.xlsx (detailed task list + owners).

Regarding credits: Laura will follow up separately with procurement to scope an appropriate commercial make-good.

Next steps:
- Please confirm the proposed weekly cadence and the Thursday slot.
- Samir: any priority verification tests you want us to run in the first canary?

Regards,
—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1-650-555-0192

Kimberly —

Thanks for the thorough write-up and the quick hot-fix. Thursday 15:00 PT works for our first checkpoint. For the canary please prioritize: (a) interactive prompt latency (user-facing p95/p99), (b) 5xx/error surface under synthetic mixed-batch load, and (c) end-to-end request traces for a set of 10 high-frequency prompt patterns we’ll share.

Procurement will expect an initial commercial proposal for credits by end of week; Laura, can you pick that up?

Appreciate the quick response.

—Samir
